top_choice_rationale: Base editing is a distinct new capability: programmed, site-specific chemical conversion of a nucleobase in living cells without double-strand cleavage, including directed evolution of a deaminase that does not exist in nature. It is mature (broad replication, first patients treated) and, with Liu alone, has a single originator and a citation that can be explained in one sentence, avoiding the Komor/Gaudelli/Nishida/Kondo allocation disputes. P003 follows because it keeps the Liu part and adds the secure nitrogenase structural core; degraders (P001) come next, limited by the missing approved drug and the glue/Sakamoto attribution problems, then nitrogenase alone (P005), then the phase-separation pairing (P004), where the physical status of many condensates is still contested.
